strategies.overview: When one looks at Deoxys-A, the first thing that stands out is its astronomical attacking stats. Its incredible base 150 Speed is also extremely relevant, as it leaves already fast Pokemon like Zacian-C, Koraidon, and Miraidon in the dust. This, in conjunction with its deep movepool, makes Deoxys-A a fearsome wallbreaker and revenge killer capable of threatening everything in the game for at least neutral damage. However, another notable aspect of Deoxys-A’s stats is its pitiful bulk that leaves it OHKOed by every attack in the game, giving it very limited opportunities to safely switch in and actually use its power, as well as leaving it prone to revenge killing from Choice Scarf users like Koraidon and Miraidon and priority from Pokemon like Extreme Killer Arceus. It also has trouble OHKOing some targets like Ting-Lu and Necrozma-DM despite its tremendous power because of a lack of either investment or STAB on its coverage. It is also significantly less threatening after it uses Psycho Boost, letting Pokemon like Miraidon and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM use it as setup fodder. Despite that, Deoxys-A is a high-reward Pokemon that is worth its high risk if played properly.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Superpower is an option on lead Deoxys-A for wearing down Ting-Lu for teammates such as Arceus-Ground, Miraidon, and Necrozma-DM. Psychic can be used over Psycho Boost to not risk a miss against Glimmora and Koraidon, but the power of Psycho Boost is useful against Arceus formes. Thunder Wave can be used to cripple opposing defensive Arceus formes and Zacian-C. On mixed attacker sets, Nasty Plot is a high-risk option that takes advantage of Deoxys-A’s ability to force switches. This usually pairs well with Focus Blast to threaten an OHKO on Ting-Lu.

Checks and Counters

Revenge Killers: While Deoxys-A is very fast, it is still outsped by some Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Koraidon and Miraidon. Flutter Mane also outspeeds Deoxys-A in sun. These Pokemon cannot switch into Deoxys-A, but they can reliably threaten to revenge kill it.

Priority: Deoxys-A's awful bulk leaves it prone to all forms of priority, such as Extreme Speed from Extreme Killer Arceus and Rayquaza, Shadow Sneak from Giratina-O, Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao and Kingambit, and Ice Shard from Chien-Pao. Tera Ghost can mitigate the weakness to Extreme Speed, but Deoxys-A cannot threaten Arceus if it is at full HP.

Psychic-resistant Pokemon: While Deoxys-A is indeed impossible to safely switch into, it is not so strong that it doesn't have any issues with power. Pokemon that resist Psycho Boost, like Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Ting-Lu, can come into it after a KO and check it, as Deoxys-A cannot OHKO these Pokemon. Necrozma-DM in particular is troublesome for Deoxys-A, as it can use Deoxys-A as setup fodder after taking Psycho Boost.

movesets.name: Mixed Attacker
movesets.description:
This set aims to get as much leverage out of Deoxys-A's limited switch-in opportunities as possible. Psycho Boost severely damages almost everything that doesn't resist it, with even defensive Ho-Oh being 2HKOed. Shadow Ball and Low Kick are mainly used to hit Pokemon that resist Psycho Boost. Shadow Ball hits enemy Psychic-types like Necrozma-DM and Calyrex-I super effectively, while Low Kick hits Zacian-C, Ting-Lu, and Kingambit on the switch. Rock Slide targets Ho-Oh, having a chance to OHKO it from full HP. Tera Ghost not only avoids revenge killing attempts from Extreme Killer Arceus but also turns Shadow Ball into a powerful attack that can serve as a strong, spammable STAB move, even OHKOing offensive Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM after minimal chip damage and doing impressive damage to defensive Necrozma-DM.

Since Deoxys-A is so frail, it requires support from pivots to get on the field safely. Therefore, Choice Scarf Koraidon and pivot Miraidon are excellent partners, as they provide reliable pivoting in the form of U-turn while being offensively threatening in their own right. They also love Deoxys-A threatening their checks. Choice Scarf Koraidon has trouble getting past physically defensive Arceus formes like Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Ground, and Arceus-Water, which Deoxys-A can break with Koraidon's U-turn support. Miraidon and Deoxys-A have common checks in healthy Ting-Lu and Arceus-Ground, so Deoxys-A pairing with Miraidon means one can work to overwhelm these checks for the other to go berserk. Entry hazard support from Gliscor and Ting-Lu is also appreciated, as it cuts down on the prediction Deoxys-A needs to actually break bulky Pokemon like Necrozma-DM and Ting-Lu. Checks to Extreme Killer Arceus and Choice Scarf Koraidon and Miraidon are also recommended, such as Zacian-C, Ting-Lu, Arceus-Ground, and Arceus-Fairy.

movesets.name: Lead
movesets.description:
Thanks to its incredibly high Special Attack and Speed, Deoxys-A is an strong alternative to Deoxys-S and Glimmora as an entry hazard setter. Shadow Ball does considerable damage to opposing Deoxys-S and Necrozma-DM. Icy Wind limits Deoxys-S to one layer of hazards while giving teammates like Miraidon and Koraidon easier entry into opposing lead Miraidon, Arceus formes, and Zacian-C. Psycho Boost is Deoxys-A’s main damage option and prevents Glimmora from getting up multiple layers of entry hazards. Taunt is another option that prevents Ribombee from setting up Sticky Web, but this is not preferred, since Ribombee often runs Pounce anyways. Stealth Rock is an option as well to let Deoxys-A set up dual hazards, but Deoxys-A’s lack of longevity and bulk means it is often limited to a single layer. Tera Ghost is the primary Tera type for giving Deoxys-A an immunity to Extreme Speed, letting it 2HKO Necrozma-DM, and for blocking Rapid Spin from Iron Treads, Great Tusk, and Terapagos. Tera Steel is also an option for blocking Glimmora's Mortal Spin.

Deoxys-A primarily fits on hyper offense for its ability to set up entry hazards and generate momentum for its teammates. Partners like Zacian-C, Miraidon, Necrozma-DM, and Koraidon appreciate Deoxys-A setting up hazards and chipping their checks, such as Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, and Arceus-Fairy. However, since Deoxys-A doesn't run Taunt often, opposing Ting-Lu leads can be difficult to deal with. Partners like Zacian-C, Koraidon, Kyurem-B, and Calyrex-I help overwhelm Ting-Lu. Furthermore, opposing Extreme Speed users such as Deoxys-S, Arceus, and Rayquaza can limit Deoxys-A to a single hazard. Teammates such as defensive Calm Mind Arceus-Ground can help take these on and provide more defensive utility to the hyper offense teams that Deoxy-A fits in. Opposing Giratina-O can anti-lead Deoxys-A and threaten teammates such as Necrozma-DM, Tera Ghost Koraidon, and Calyrex-I, so partners like Chien-Pao, Miraidon and Kyurem-B that can threaten it out are appreciated.

movesets.name: All-Out Attacker
movesets.description: These are sample sets while we work on the full analyses. Stay tuned for updates as the metagame develops.

movesets.name: Glass Cannon
movesets.description:
• Deoxys-A's out-of-this-world offensive stats and good coverage give it a niche over Focus Sash Calyrex-S as a glass cannon.

  • Psycho Boost: Even with minimal investment, Psycho Boost deals massive damage to anything that doesn't resist it. It's also Deoxys-A's way of OHKOing Koraidon and 2HKOing Dondozo.

  • Low Kick: Since Deoxys-A has such a short lifespan, Low Kick's lack of offensive drops makes it preferred over Superpower. This is especially because Superpower's two biggest targets, Ting-Lu and Arceus, take just as much damage from Low Kick anyways.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off does a brilliant job of letting Deoxys-A revenge kill common Choice Scarf foes like Miraidon, in addition to being good coverage against Calyrex-S and Lunala.

  • Extreme Speed: Despite Deoxys-A's incredible Speed, Extreme Speed is still useful for picking off weakened priority users like Arceus and Dragonite.

  • Using Pressure for Speed Scouting: While Pressure may seem laughable on such a frail glass cannon, it can be very useful in lead situations to determine if certain Pokemon are carrying a Choice Scarf or not. For example, if Miraidon and Koraidon's abilities activate before Deoxys-A's Pressure does, this means that they are carrying a Choice Scarf! Just note that this tactic does not work against the Calyrex formes, as their abilities always activate first.

  • EV Spreads - Physical Offense versus Special Offense: Focusing on physical offense gets the most out of Deoxys-A after Psycho Boost has powered it down, but focusing on special offense turns Deoxys-A into more of a hit-and-run wallbreaker, especially when paired with Tera Psychic.

Other Options

  • Rock Slide: While not very powerful, this is Deoxys-A's best shot of burying Ho-Oh.

  • Stealth Rock: Deoxys-A's suicide lead-like nature makes Stealth Rock a natural seeming fit, but it can be difficult to justify over better coverage or the ability to revenge kill with Extreme Speed.

  • Expanding Force: This deals tremendous damage if you're pairing Deoxys-A with Indeedee-M, though losing out on coverage can still be an issue because Psycho Boost shouldn't be replaced.

  • Superpower: Superpower hits lighter foes such as Chi-Yu much harder than Low Kick and can fit especially well on more specially offensive variants of Deoxys-A.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 116 Atk / 252 SpA / 140 Spe with Rash: While giving up the matchups against Jolly Chien-Pao and Timid Flutter Mane is a shame, the extra Special Attack with a Rash nature lets Deoxys-A OHKO physically defensive Landorus-T with Tera Psychic Psycho Boost and still outspeed Adamant Chien-Pao.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Deoxys-A will usually only Terastallize if a sweep is in sight or to give itself a useful immunity. Otherwise, Deoxys-A usually doesn't survive long enough to make amazing use of Terastallization.

  • Normal: Tera Normal fits physically offensive Deoxys-A the best, boosting Extreme Speed for picking off weakened threats and punishing Choice-locked Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane.

  • Psychic: If you're using specially offensive Deoxys-A, Tera Psychic Psycho Boost tears through new foes like Flutter Mane and offensive Miriadon.

  • Stellar: Since Deoxys-A is snuffed out so fast, Tera Stellar's one-time boost isn't as much of a concern. This is especially true for specially offensive sets that aren't as focused on potential sweeps with Extreme Speed.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost stops Arceus and Dragonite from sniping Deoxys-A with Extreme Speed.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is specifically used to punish Koraidon that attempt to set up by Terastallizing and using Scale Shot.

movesets.name: Mixed Attacker
movesets.description:
• Deoxys-A's unrivaled power, great coverage, and amazing Speed tier let it serve as an almost unwallable mid-to-late-game wallbreaker that can also double as a revenge killer.

  • Psycho Boost OHKOes offensive Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Eternatus, Rayquaza, and Zygarde, while being able to OHKO Terastallized offensive Eternatus and Zygarde after slight chip damage.

  • Low Kick has consistently high Base Power thanks to the high general weight of Pokemon in National Dex Ubers, and it 2HKOes Dark-type Pokemon like Arceus-Dark and offensive Yveltal without any drawbacks. Low Kick also hits Necrozma-DM for a reasonable amount of damage and does large amounts of damage into certain specially bulky Pokemon like Primal Kyogre.

  • Shadow Ball has virtually perfect neutral coverage with Low Kick and hits Necrozma-DM, which otherwise is not particularly threatened by Deoxys-A's moves, for a 2HKO. With Tera Ghost, Shadow Ball becomes genuinely powerful, allowing it to OHKO Mega Mewtwo Y, Ultra Necrozma, and Necrozma-DM after a layer of Spikes, and 2HKO almost everything it hits neutrally. It should be noted, however, that a super effective Shadow Ball is weaker than a neutral Psycho Boost unless Terastallization is used, which can make Deoxys-A a bit reliant on such a mechanic to act as a proper wallbreaker in these matchups.

  • At the cost of making Deoxys-A reliant on Terastallization to use Ghost-type coverage, running Tera Blast over Shadow Ball makes Deoxys-A much less exploitable overall. Due to becoming physical after Psycho Boost is used and coming off of Deoxys-A's base 180 Attack, Tera Blast is barely weakened, and it can confirm a KO on a badly poisoned Ho-Oh switching into Psycho Boost—making running dedicated coverage for Ho-Oh much less necessary—while still being incredibly difficult to switch into. Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C are still 2HKOed by a physical Tera Blast Ghost, and physical Tera Blast also retains the ability to OHKO Ultra Necrozma, Mega Mewtwo Y, and offensive Lunala, preventing these threats from exploiting Deoxys-A.

  • Running Rock Slide allows Deoxys-A to potentially OHKO defensive Ho-Oh, dissuading it from consistently sponging attacks from Deoxys-A and allowing Deoxys-A to defeat it one-on-one. Because Rock Slide is physical, it can safely be used after Psycho Boost is used, increasing its general consistency. It also hits Yveltal harder than Low Kick, notably 2HKOing defensive variants.

  • Ice Beam hits Yveltal harder than Rock Slide, OHKOing all variants after Stealth Rock, while relieving Deoxys-A of the need to use Psycho Boost to OHKO targets like Zygarde, Mega Salamence, and Rayquaza.

  • Extreme Speed is a third option over Rock Slide that gives Deoxys-A more play against offensive teams. Not only does it allow Deoxys-A to revenge kill weakened Speed boosters like Ultra Necrozma and Mega Salamence, but it also allows Deoxys-A to prevent Ditto from revenge killing it via Tera Ghost + Extreme Speed and gives Deoxys-A counterplay against Sucker Punch Yveltal.

  • A Naive nature with 252 Speed EVs is ran to ensure that Deoxys-A outspeeds Zacian-C and Mega Mewtwo Y, allowing it to threaten them. The Speed also allows Deoxys-A Speed tie opposing Deoxys-A and outspeed slower foes at +1, such as Necrozma-DM and Zygarde. 29 HP IVs reduce Life Orb recoil.

  • In addition to the offensive power boost to Deoxys-A's Ghost-type coverage, Tera Ghost gives Deoxys-A an immunity to Extreme Speed, allowing it to check Arceus and Rayquaza. In certain cases, however, Tera Normal may be considered to blank Marshadow while allowing Psycho Boost + Extreme Speed to often KO Ho-Oh from full health, but the immunity is otherwise useless and doing this denies Deoxys-A the option of having powerful Ghost-type coverage, making it easier to handle overall.

  • Because Deoxys-A is absurdly frail, it should never be brought into an attack, lest it get OHKOed. Instead, it should be brought in via the use of double switches, after a Pokemon is KOed, or via a slow pivot. It should also only be attacking if it can OHKO the target or if a switch is predicted.

  • Deoxys-A can be extremely reliant on entry hazards and general chip damage to secure many notable OHKOs, so hazard setters like Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, and Eternatus are good partners.

  • Deoxys-A is easily revenge killed by Marshadow and checked by Dark-types like Yveltal—particularly Sucker Punch variants—and Arceus-Dark, so Pokemon that handle them well like Arceus-Fairy and support variants of Yveltal are useful teammates. The former can also be handy against Arceus-Dark and Yveltal, which can otherwise be a great hinderance to Deoxys-A, while the latter is a rare source of pivoting in U-turn, which can be used to give Deoxys-A additional wallbreaking opportunities.

movesets.name: Lead
movesets.description:
• Having wide coverage to bluff offensive pressure alongside a Speed tier above the vast majority of the metagame, Deoxys-A can act as a formidable entry hazard setter that can also compress roles as a wallbreaker, filling a niche of hyper offense teams.

  • Psycho Boost acts as a strong STAB move that limits Glimmora to only set a single entry hazard at most, and has high odds to OHKO Eruption Primal Groudon. Counter is an alternative to OHKO foes such as Necrozma-DM and Ho-Oh after luring an attack while having its Focus Sash intact, giving a means for Deoxys-A to play around such checks.

  • Shadow Ball provides coverage to super effectively target anti-leads such as Necrozma-DM and Deoxys-S, avoiding passivity and giving the rest of its team an easier chance to break past them by wearing them down.

  • Icy Wind allows Deoxys-A to anti-lead Deoxys-S, enabling Deoxys-A to outspeed and KO it with Shadow Ball afterwards. This move can also be used to wear down setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, rendering them easier to revenge kill by mitigating their Speed stat boosts.

  • Tera Steel grants an immunity to Glimmora's Mortal Spin, giving the situational use to preserve entry hazards on the other side of the field.

  • By keeping Deoxys-A for the middle stages of the game instead of leading with it, it can bluff as another set variant of itself, allowing it to set entry hazards mid-game on expected switches. This strategy is usually ideal if the foe is likely to lead with a Pokemon that Deoxys-A can't play around depending on its set, such as Yveltal for sets without Icy Wind, and Grimmsnarl for any variant outside of Taunt, but entry hazards should be kept out of its side of the field to ensure Deoxys-A can use its Focus Sash.

  • As the offensive pressure of Deoxys-A relies on forcing the opponent to scout its moveset, it's best to not unecessarily reveal parts of its moveset unless the situation calls for it.

  • Deoxys-A can struggle to get past Defoggers such as Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Arceus-Dark, and Steel-types including Necrozma-DM and Ferrothorn, therefore allies such as Zacian-C, Marshadow, and Double Dance Primal Groudon make great allies to wallbreak past them.

  • Hyper offense Pokemon such as Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, and Eternatus appreciate the entry hazards laid by Deoxys-A to more often threaten the opposing team with a sweep by wearing down their checks and punishing switching.

movesets.name: Meteor Beam
movesets.description:
• Meteor Beam Deoxys-A is an excellent wallbreaker and sweeper thanks to its massive Special Attack stat, great Speed tier, and extensive offensive coverage for Psychic Terrain teams.

  • Expanding Force is an extremely powerful option under Psychic Terrain, having a chance to 3HKO Chansey at +1. Psycho Boost is Deoxys-A’s most powerful Psychic-type STAB move, providing Deoxys-A with a strong wallbreaking attack even when Psychic Terrain isn’t active. Psycho Boost OHKOes Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy, defensive Arceus-Water, and wallbreaker Primal Kyogre at +1 after two layers of Spikes.

  • Focus Blast provides essential coverage against Arceus-Dark and Zacian-C. Shadow Ball and Dark Pulse are both options for coverage against Necrozma-DM. If Deoxys-A is Tera Ghost, Shadow Ball should be chosen for the increased boost, as it guarantees a 2HKO on Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Otherwise, Dark Pulse should be chosen due to its flinch chance.

  • Tera Psychic allows Deoxys-A to OHKO Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy, defensive Arceus-Water, and Wallbreaker Primal Kyogre with Psycho Boost at +1, and OHKO Ho-Oh at +1 under Psychic Terrain. For Expanding Force, Tera Psychic gives Deoxys-A a chance to 2HKO Chansey under Psychic Terrain at +1. However, Tera Psychic leaves Deoxys-A susceptible to priority if Psychic Terrain isn’t active.

  • Tera Ghost allows Deoxys-A to avoid being revenge killed by Extreme Speed from Arceus and Rayquaza while also boosting Shadow Ball. Tera Normal prevents Marshadow and Giratina-O from revenge killing it with Shadow Sneak.

  • As Deoxys-A is a potent wallbreaker even without a boost, it does not need to use Meteor Beam until the prime opportunity for a sweep, such as when its checks in Yveltal or Ho-Oh have been baited in.

  • As Deoxys-A is extremely frail, it should only switch in on a free turn such as after a teammate faints. On Psychic Terrain teams, it is best to sacrifice Tapu Lele as a means to give Deoxys-A a free switch in and maximize the time it can take advantage of Psychic Terrain.

  • Tapu Lele is an essential teammate for Psychic Terrain, as it is the most viable setter. Meteor Beam Lunala pairs well with Deoxys-A on Psychic Terrain teams, as the two of them can overwhelm Yveltal and Ho-Oh defensive cores. With Lunala eliminating one of these threats, Deoxys-A is free to use its Meteor Beam to eliminate the other part of the core without worrying about being stopped in the middle of a sweep afterwards.

  • Glimmora is an excellent teammate for Deoxys-A, as the entry hazard it provides eases sweeping. In addition, Toxic Spikes is able to chip Arceus-Dark, which puts it in Focus Blast range. In return, Deoxys-A is able to threaten common Defoggers such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal. Smeargle and Shuckle can be used instead to provide Sticky Web, as this greatly aids other Psychic Terrain teammates such as Lunala and Basculegion.
